versions.short: The resolution designates September 2026 as National Child Awareness Month to promote awareness of charities that benefit children and youth-serving organizations across the United States. It recognizes the work these charities and organizations do for children and youth as critical contributions to the country's future. It also stresses the importance of meeting the needs of children and youth, including those who have experienced homelessness, are in foster care, are at risk of or have been victims of child sex trafficking, have been affected by violence or trauma, or have serious physical or mental health needs. It further highlights the value of arts and cultural opportunities and educational programs that address learning gaps.
